notes:
The table has 196 entries. Match order is part of the data: run through the array in order and take the first entry whose substring appears in the lower-cased renderer or adapter string. The matching should first strip or accept the (r) and (tm) marks. Specific names are listed before general ones: laptop before desktop, Ti Super before Ti before plain, XTX before XT, RX 6600M before RX 6600, RX 5700 before RX 570, Apple Mx Max/Pro before Mx, A18 Pro before A18, uhd graphics before hd graphics, nvidia a100 before nvidia a10, and L40S/L40 before L4. Catch-all entries ("apple gpu", "adreno", "mali") come last.

How browsers report names:
- **Chrome on Windows** returns an ANGLE string such as "angle (nvidia, nvidia geforce rtx 4070 laptop gpu (0x...) direct3d11...)".
- **Chrome on Mac** returns "angle (apple, angle metal renderer: apple m2 pro, ...)".
- **Safari** (all iOS/iPadOS browsers) and often Firefox return only "apple gpu" or a generic string. iPhone chips (A14 to A20) usually cannot be matched by name, so the app will need other hints such as screen size or WebGPU limits. The A-series entries are for when a real name shows up.
- **Turing laptop GPUs** that are not Max-Q report desktop names (e.g. "rtx 2070"), so they will slightly overstate bandwidth.

Where one name covers several VRAM variants (RTX 4060 Ti 8/16, 5060 Ti 16/8, 3060 12/8, 3080 10/12, 3080 Laptop 8/16, 1060 6/3, RX 9060 XT 16/8), the table uses the most common one and the name says so.

Unconfirmed figures and estimates:
- **Qualcomm Adreno X2-90** is set to 152 GB/s, the 128-bit X2 Elite. The X2 Elite Extreme has the same GPU name but 228 GB/s over a 192-bit LPDDR5X-9523 bus (Qualcomm brief / Chips and Cheese), and the two cannot be told apart from the string.
- **Integrated and mobile bandwidth** is the typical platform's system memory figure (bus bits / 8 × MT/s):
  - 780M: about 90 GB/s. It ranges from DDR5-5600 at 89.6 up to LPDDR5X-7500 at 120.
  - 880M/890M: LPDDR5X-7500, about 120 GB/s.
  - Lunar Lake: LPDDR5X-8533, 136 GB/s.
  - Panther Lake B390/B370: LPDDR5X-9600, about 153 GB/s. Estimate.
  - Snapdragon 8 Elite / Elite Gen 5: 64-bit LPDDR5X-10667, about 85 GB/s.
  - 8 Gen 3: about 77 GB/s.
  - 8 Gen 2: about 68 GB/s.
- **A19 Pro and A20 Pro** bandwidth (about 77 GB/s) are estimates from LPDDR5X-9600.
- **Tensor G5 PowerVR** figures, **Xclipse 950/960** figures and **mobile GPU TFLOPS** are rough estimates.
- **fp16_tflops** is the non-tensor shader rate. NVIDIA Ampere and later run FP16 at the FP32 rate, Turing and GTX 16 at 2×, and Pascal at 1/64 (hence tiny numbers; llama.cpp uses FP32 there). For RDNA3/4 it is the dual-issue ×2 figure, which is optimistic. Apple entries are listed at FP32 ≈ FP16.
